ERM differs from traditional risk management by taking a holistic approach to managing risk.
As part of the ERM program, the University procures appropriate insurance as one of many risk control and mitigation measures.
The University is insured for various risks of loss arising out of claims for negligence, including bodily injury and property damage, wrongful acts, cyber liability, professional liability and workers compensation through a combination of insurance polici es and self -insurance.

Review of the Governor’s FY2027 Recommended Budget Enclosure Abby Benson, Vice President, Administration and Finance Vice President for Administration and Finance Abby Benson discussed the Governor’s FY27 Recommended Budget (GRB), which was released on January 15, 2026.
Vice President Benson reminded the Committee that the release of the GRB is the first step in the process that concludes when the legislature approves the budget, often at the very end of the legislative session (June).
Vice President Benson’s presentation included a comparison of the FY26 and FY27 requests, with specific detail on requests to cover the Operating Budget shortfall, support the Current Service Level, and support of Strategic Initiatives.
Out of a request for an increase of $37.6M to operating costs, URI was provided only a $4.2M increase related solely to Current Service Levels. (Details can be found in the enclosure.).

Regarding the request for support for Strategic Initiatives, Committee members asked if URI had ever received requested funds.
Vice President Benson noted that funds were partially provided once in FY24, specifically for Blue Economy projects.
However, the University continues to request this support from the state to signal the University’s ongoing commitments to these efforts.
She also noted that the University continues to support many of these initiatives regardless of direct state appropriations, through reallocation of existing resources, because they represent critical efforts for the University.
Upon questions from the Committee, Vice President Benson also noted that there is no federal support for many URI financial aid initiatives (e.g., National Guard support, Talent Development).
Vice President Benson discussed the projected FY26 budget shortfall, noting that current mid-year projections no longer show a shortfall (it had been projected at ~$3.8M).
However, this shift is primarily due to the current hiring freeze implemented in order to stay within the full-time equivalent (FTE) cap.

Vice President Benson also discussed the increased RICAP funds in the GRB, noting that URI asked for $17.3M and received (a proposed) $15.2M.
She noted that additionally, the GRB included $1.6M for access control projects, $9.0M for ADA projects, and $21.0M for building envelope projects, with indications of ongoing annual support for the latter two categories.

Requests for Carothers HVAC ($67.6M), Allen Harbor Bulkhead and Dock replacement ($6.7M), and Public Safety Building ($48.3M) were not recommended for funding in the GRB.
Importantly, the GRB did recommend that URI not be subject to the FTE cap, retroactively to July 1, 2025.
Vice President Benson noted that while this is very good news, this change needs to be approved by the state legislature.

President DATE: June 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the FY2028―FY2032 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2028―FY2032 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island, which the committee reviewed at its April meeting.
The CIP, due in July of each year, is the first FY28 budget submittal in the cycle and is a five-year rolling plan of proposed University capital projects of $1.0M or greater, using unrestricted funds together with related requests for State funding.
Points to Consider: The enclosed presentation provides updates to existing CIP projects' scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 2, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, Student Success, and the Public Safety Building.

It also provides information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects, which are both now scheduled for reactivation following our successful P3 Housing project outcome.
The presentation also highlights several projects, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions include the refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems , the university’s water tower , Allen Harbor bulkhead and dock replacement, and the NBC shoreline stabilization project.
Two new projects are proposed to be added to the CIP this year : including a new Graduate School of Oceanography (GSO) Marine Operations Building, including renovations to the Aquarium Ark, to support the new R/V NARRAGANSETT DAWN, and the renovation of the Middleton building on the NBC to provide spaces for the GSO Marine Geological Samples Laboratory and the Facilities.
The CIP also recommends a 2028 General Obligation (GO) Bond project for Student Success.

Although currently envisioned as a standalone facility on the site of the Carlotti Building, we will investigate the opportunity to move this program into the Carothers’ Library as we reenvision how the library is best used to support the ongoing needs of our campus community.

Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2028―FY2032. Supporting Information: Please see University of Rhode Island FY 2028- FY2032 CIP Enclosure. TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: February 2, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Consideration of a Resolution on Bond Reimbursement Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the Board of Trustees for a resolution allowing for the reimbursement of expenditures related to two infrastructure projects that may be made by the University prior to the issuance of debt supporting these projects.
The University anticipates seeking authorization from the Board to issue a revenue bond in fall 2026 to support both projects.
The proposed reimbursement amount would be capped at $6.91M, which equals the portion of the project costs anticipated to be spent between now and bond issuance, with a 15% contingency buffer.

The two projects are: 1) Utility Infrastructure Upgrade – Phase III (total project cost: $9.1M) 2) Repaving and Hardscape Improvements (total project cost: $20M) Points to Consider: URI has a history of funding capital expenditures through the issuance of tax-exempt bonds, repayment of which is made over a period of years that does not exceed the useful life of the capital assets being financed.
These tax- exempt bonds are subject to federal regulations that, among other matters, limit arbitrage or require rebate of earnings in certain circumstances and require ongoing compliance.
Federal tax regulations provide that the University can advance its own funds to pay capital expenditures prior to the issuance of tax-exempt bonds, use such bond proceeds to reimburse itself for the advanced funds, and treat such bond proceeds as being “spent” for federal tax purposes when the reimbursement is made, thus avoiding further tax compliance with respect to such funds.

To avail itself of the ability to make such reimbursement, under the applicable tax regulations, the University must declare its “official intent” prior to making the capital expenditures expected to be reimbursed from bond proceeds.
URI is seeking this declaration of “official intent” from the Board to reimburse itself for funds related to two projects currently on the University’s Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) that will be debt-financed through revenue bonds contemplated to be issued in Fall 2026, pending Board of Trustees approval.
These two projects would begin in summer 2026.
URI has already received Kushner authorization to issue th e Utility Infrastructure Phase III project bond, and the Kushner for the Parking and Repaving project is included in the FY27 Governor’s request and is currently under review by the General Assembly.

The projected expenditures proposed for reimbursement for the Utility Infrastructure Phase III project is $4.51M, to replace the Farmhouse Road Steam line. The projected expenditures for the Parking and Hardscape project, to replace parking lost by the construction of a new residence hall, is $1.5M. The total amount of projected reimbursement is $6.01M. We have added a 15% contingency buffer to this amount to request a total reimbursable amount of $6.91M If approved, the University would create a dedicated reimbursable fund for these two projects and expenditures would be made using University reserves, which reserves would be replenished upon reimbursement from the proceeds of the revenue bond. Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the resolution to allow for the reimbursement of certain expenditures made prior to the issuance of the bond funding the projects noted here. Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT the University hereby declares its official intent pursuant to Section 1.150- 2 of the Treasury Regulations to use proceeds of tax-exempt bonds, issued by the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation, to reimburse the University for capital expenditures in connection with the following projects: 1) Utility Infrastructure Upgrade – Phase III; and 2) Repaving and Hardscape Improvements, paid prior to the issuance of such new bonds, if any, in an amount not greater than $6,910,000. This declaration does not bind the University to make any expenditure, incur any indebtedness for new money projects, or t o proceed with the new money projects.
